Bug_Title: INT: Bad comparison of signed byte (INT_BAD_COMPARISON_WITH_SIGNED_BYTE)
Bug_Details:
Signed bytes can only have a value in the range -128 to 127. Comparing
a signed byte with a value outside that range is vacuous and likely to be incorrect.
To convert a signed byte b to an unsigned value in the range 0..255,
use 0xff & b.
 b 0xff & b
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by comparing a signed byte 'b' with the value 200. Since the maximum value a signed byte can hold is 127, any comparison with a value greater than 127 is vacuously false and indicates a logical error.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case triggered the bug by calling the showBug method with a byte value of 200. Since the method compares the byte with 200, which is outside the range of a signed byte (-128 to 127), the comparison is vacuously false but the code incorrectly returns true, causing the test to fail.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that both tests passed successfully without any failures. The test 'testShowBugWithLargeValue' was expected to fail due to the bug, but it did not. This suggests that the bug did not trigger as expected based on the provided test results.
